summary: Marco Ferrante specializes in Indology and philosophy. He earned his bachelor's and PhD at Sapienza University of Rome. He held posts at the Austrian Academy of Sciences, Sapienza University of Rome, the University of Oxford, and the University of Vienna.

Marco Franceschini is an Indologist who earned his PhD from the University of Turin. He served as an assistant professor (attested 2019) and became an associate professor in 2021 at the University of Bologna.

Marco Trombetta works in Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. He earned his PhD at Seoul National University (2009–2023) and held a post at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation.
Marco Walther is a scholar in Tibetology. He completed his PhD at the University of Munich, where he studied under doctoral supervisor Franz-Karl Ehrhard.

Marco della Tomba (1726–1803) worked in Indology and religious studies. He served as a missionary in the Tibet-Hindustan Mission (1757–1773), and later as Propraefectus (1786) and Praefectus (1801) of the Tibet Mission.

Marcus Bingenheimer works in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and computational fields. He studied at Würzburg, Nagoya under Yasuhisa Matsumura, Heidelberg, and under Huinan Yang. He held posts at Dharma Drum Institute, Chung-Hwa Institute, and Temple University.

Marcus Joseph Müller (1809–1874) studied Iranian and Central Asian studies, Indology, and religious studies at Munich under Othmar Frank, Leiden, and Paris. He became professor of Non-Biblical Oriental Literature at the University of Munich.

Marek Mejor works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied under Eugeniusz Słuszkiewicz at the University of Warsaw, later serving as professor there (attested 2000–2010), and held a fellowship at Wolfson College, Oxford (1981–1982).

Marek Zemánek specializes in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He completed studies at Dongguk University, Seoul National University, and Charles University, where he prepared his dissertation under doctoral supervisor Radek Chlup (attested 2017).
Marek Zvelebil (1952–2011) was a scholar in history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Sheffield and held a post there from circa 1981 to 2011.
Margaret Cone is a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies who taught Dhivan Thomas Jones. She held posts at the University of Cambridge and Darwin College, Cambridge (both attested 1996).
Margaret Elizabeth Noble (1867–1911) was a scholar in religious studies and Indology. She studied at Halifax Ladies' College and under Swami Vivekananda as her traditional teacher in 1898.
Margaret Gouin specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She completed her PhD at the University of Bristol, where she studied under doctoral supervisor Paul Williams.

Margaret H. Dornish works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. She studied at Yale University, Claremont Graduate University, and the University of Southern California, and served as Associate Professor of Religion at Pomona College (attested 1989).

Margaret Mead (1901–1978) studied at DePauw, Barnard, and Columbia under Franz Boas. She worked at the American Museum of Natural History, Columbia, Fordham, RAND Corporation, The New School, and the University of Rhode Island.

Margaret R. Miles is a religious studies and history scholar. Educated at San Francisco State and the Graduate Theological Union, she taught at Harvard Divinity School and served as dean at GTU and president of the American Academy of Religion.

Margarethe Steiner (b. 1872) was an Indology scholar. She earned her PhD at the University of Tübingen under Richard von Garbe in 1926, and later studied under Jakob Wilhelm Hauer and held a post there in 1939.

Margarita Angelica Delgado Creamer works in religious studies and Sinology. She completed her PhD under Linda Penkower at the University of Pittsburgh, where she also held a post, and had postdoctoral mentoring from Xiuping Hong.

Margarita Iosifovna Vorobyova-Desyatovskaya (1933–2021) worked in Buddhist, Indology, and Central Asian studies. Educated at St. Petersburg University, she held long-term posts at the Institute of Oriental Studies and Institute of Oriental Manuscripts, and visited Soka University.
Margarita Kleibel is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied under teacher Karin Preisendanz and completed her master's degree under supervisor Klaus-Dieter Mathes.
